modals.install_claude_statusline_message: Token Use will write a wrapper script to your config directory and update ~/.claude/settings.json (with a timestamped backup) so that Claude Code calls the wrapper. Your existing statusLine command, if any, will still run inside the wrapper so the visible status line is unchanged.
modals.install_claude_statusline_manual_message: Token Use will write the wrapper script only. You'll need to point statusLine.command in ~/.claude/settings.json at it yourself.
modals.uninstall_claude_statusline_message: Token Use will restore your previous statusLine.command (or remove the entry if none was set) and delete the wrapper script. The sidecar limits file is left in place.
modals.codex_subscription_limits_source: chatgpt.com wham usage endpoint (session cookie required)

modals.claude_subscription_limits_effect: reads the keychain session cookie, writes a local quota snapshot, then syncs archive limits

modals.download_latest_rates_message: This will download the latest published Token Use currency snapshot into your local config directory.
modals.download_latest_prices_message: This will download the latest pricing books into your local config directory.
modals.sync_copilot_limits_message: This will read your locally stored Copilot OAuth token or authenticated GitHub CLI session, fetch current Copilot quota state from GitHub, and write it into your local config directory.
modals.clear_data_message: Token Use will delete archive.db, rebuild it from local tool history, and keep config, rates, pricing, limits, and reports. Rows whose source files are gone will not return.

lazy-prompting.name: Lazy Prompting
lazy-prompting.description: Very short prompts rarely give the model enough context to produce quality results.
lazy-prompting.how_to_improve: Describe the intent, constraints, and expected output instead of one-liners.

caps-lock.name: Caps Lock Rage
caps-lock.description: Messages written almost entirely in capitals signal frustration, not intent.
caps-lock.when_triggered: {count} prompts were written mostly in CAPS.
caps-lock.how_to_improve: Step away, take a breath, then return with a calm, structured prompt.

frustration-signals.name: Frustration Signals
frustration-signals.description: Excessive punctuation or shouting usually means the current approach is not working.
frustration-signals.when_triggered: {count} prompts show frustration indicators (!!!, ???, ALL CAPS).
frustration-signals.how_to_improve: Change strategy instead of escalating: start a fresh session, rephrase, or split the problem.

repeated-prompts.name: Repeated Prompts
repeated-prompts.description: Near-duplicate prompts spend tokens without producing new results.
repeated-prompts.when_triggered: {count} prompts are near-duplicates across {stat} distinct messages.
repeated-prompts.how_to_improve: If a prompt did not work, rephrase it or add context rather than retrying it verbatim.

low-constraint-usage.name: Low Constraint Usage
low-constraint-usage.description: Constraints narrow the output space and produce higher-quality code.
low-constraint-usage.when_triggered: Only {pct} of substantial prompts include constraint language ({stat} of {total}).
low-constraint-usage.how_to_improve: Add explicit constraints: "do not touch the public API", "only use std", "limit to 50 lines".

verbose-output.name: Verbose Model Output
verbose-output.description: Huge answers to tiny prompts burn output tokens without proportional value.
verbose-output.when_triggered: {count} turns ({pct}) produced 5K+ output tokens from prompts under 200 characters.
verbose-output.how_to_improve: Ask for concise answers or set an output format; add output constraints for routine tasks.

verbose-prompt-no-compression.name: Verbose Prompts
verbose-prompt-no-compression.description: Long, filler-heavy prompts inflate input tokens on every turn.
verbose-prompt-no-compression.when_triggered: {count} prompts ({pct}) are 800+ characters with two or more filler words.
verbose-prompt-no-compression.how_to_improve: Be terse and structured: bullet points beat paragraphs, and pleasantries cost tokens.

excessive-file-context.name: Excessive File Context
excessive-file-context.description: Bulk-attaching files pays for context the model mostly never reads.
excessive-file-context.how_to_improve: Attach the 3-5 most relevant files and let the agent search for the rest on demand.

session-drift.name: Session Drift
session-drift.description: Sessions that mix many task types muddy the context window.
session-drift.when_triggered: {count} sessions cover four or more different work types.
session-drift.how_to_improve: Start a new session when switching task type - focused sessions get better responses.

late-night-coding.name: Late-Night Coding
late-night-coding.description: Late-night work correlates with more bugs and lower-quality output.
late-night-coding.how_to_improve: Consider healthier working hours; quality drops sharply when fatigued.

weekend-overwork.name: Weekend Overwork
weekend-overwork.description: A high weekend share may indicate work-life balance issues.
weekend-overwork.how_to_improve: Keep boundaries between work and personal time - sustained overwork leads to burnout.

mega-sessions.name: Mega Sessions
mega-sessions.description: Very long sessions degrade context quality and response accuracy.
mega-sessions.how_to_improve: Start new sessions periodically; break large tasks into focused conversations.

abandon-sessions.name: Abandoned Sessions
abandon-sessions.description: Single-message sessions leave refinement on the table.
abandon-sessions.when_triggered: {count} sessions ({pct}) ended after a single turn.
abandon-sessions.how_to_improve: Iterate with follow-ups - refining a response beats one-shot prompting.

high-cancellation.name: Excessive Cancellations
high-cancellation.description: Frequent interrupts waste quota and usually mean unclear prompting.
high-cancellation.how_to_improve: Write clearer, more specific prompts, and let responses finish before redirecting.

broken-flow-state.name: Broken Flow State
broken-flow-state.description: Fragmented days with scattered prompts point to context switches and interruptions.
broken-flow-state.when_triggered: {count} of {total} active days ({pct}) show fragmented flow (avg score {stat}).
broken-flow-state.how_to_improve: Protect 2+ hour blocks, silence notifications, and pre-plan the next prompt while the agent works.

slow-responses.name: Slow Responses
slow-responses.description: Consistently slow turns often mean overly broad prompts.
slow-responses.how_to_improve: Break complex asks into smaller, focused requests.

runaway-agent-loops.name: Runaway Agent Loops
runaway-agent-loops.description: Turns with an extreme number of tool calls suggest the agent is spinning on a failing approach.
runaway-agent-loops.how_to_improve: If the agent loops, interrupt and rephrase with clearer constraints or a smaller scope.

copy-paste-blindness.name: Copy-Paste Blindness
copy-paste-blindness.description: Large AI output accepted without any follow-up usually means it shipped unreviewed.
copy-paste-blindness.when_triggered: {count} sessions produced 50+ AI LoC with no refinement afterwards.
copy-paste-blindness.how_to_improve: Review generated code before accepting - ask follow-ups, test, and adjust.

speed-accept.name: Speed Accept
speed-accept.description: Moving on within seconds of receiving a large diff is not a review.
speed-accept.when_triggered: {count} times the next message came within 15s of 20+ lines of AI code (avg {stat}).
speed-accept.how_to_improve: Read the code: correctness, security, and edge cases deserve more than a glance.

vibe-coding.name: Vibe Coding
vibe-coding.description: High AI output from a handful of vague prompts creates knowledge debt.
vibe-coding.when_triggered: {count} sessions generated {stat}+ AI LoC from five or fewer unstructured prompts.
vibe-coding.how_to_improve: Write a small spec first and review output line by line - velocity without understanding is debt.

tunnel-vision.name: Single-Project Tunnel Vision
tunnel-vision.description: AI assistance concentrated in one project leaves the rest of your workflow unassisted.
tunnel-vision.how_to_improve: Use the assistant across other projects too: docs, tests, DevOps, exploration.

no-language-exploration.name: No Language Exploration
no-language-exploration.description: AI dramatically lowers the cost of trying a new language - unused, that advantage lapses.
no-language-exploration.when_triggered: No new language in {count} weeks ({stat} languages seen overall).
no-language-exploration.how_to_improve: Ask for something small in a language you have never used - the barrier has never been lower.

mcp-tool-bloat.name: Tool / MCP Bloat
mcp-tool-bloat.description: Very large active toolsets add silent context overhead to every prompt.
mcp-tool-bloat.how_to_improve: Trim rarely-used MCP servers and scope toolsets per project.

model-overreliance.name: Model Overreliance
model-overreliance.description: One model for everything means overpaying for simple tasks.
model-overreliance.how_to_improve: Route lighter tasks to cheaper models and keep premium models for real reasoning.

reasoning-effort-overuse.name: Reasoning Effort Overuse
reasoning-effort-overuse.description: High or max reasoning effort bills extra thinking tokens even when the task does not need them.
reasoning-effort-overuse.when_triggered: {count} of {total} effort-tagged turns ({pct}) ran at high or max effort.
reasoning-effort-overuse.how_to_improve: Default to medium effort and escalate only for genuinely hard problems.

premium-waste.name: Premium Model Waste
premium-waste.description: Short lookup-style questions rarely benefit from premium-priced models.
premium-waste.when_triggered: {count} trivial or lookup-style turns ran on premium models.
premium-waste.how_to_improve: Send quick questions to lighter models; reserve premium models for complex generation.

cache-hit-starvation.name: Prompt Cache Starvation
cache-hit-starvation.description: Long prompts that miss the cache pay full price for context the model has already seen.
cache-hit-starvation.when_triggered: {count} long-prompt turns served only {stat} of input from cache.
cache-hit-starvation.how_to_improve: Keep prompt prefixes stable: short stable instructions, file references over pasted code, fewer mid-task resets.
